Subject: Hosted API — data locality & retention questions

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. Our security team put together a short set of clarifying questions focused on where data lives, retention windows, and deletion guarantees for the Hosted API. Can you confirm the following for production tenant data and optional logs?

1) Can production request payloads be pinned to a US-only region for both storage and processing?
2) What is Redwood's default retention for request/response content and any derived embeddings if enabled?
3) How are deletion requests handled for a tenant (timeline + evidence)?
4) Do backups/snapshots ever leave the geo-boundary or are they encrypted with customer KMS?

If you prefer, a short PDF with each answer plus references to docs and compliance artifacts would be ideal. We need this for our vendor review by Oct 22.

Regards,
Rajiv
Director, Cloud Security — Horizon Health
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Hi Rajiv — thanks for the clear list. I put together concise answers below and attached a short PDF pack for your security review (HostedAPI_Data_Locality_Answers_v1.2.pdf) and the populated spreadsheet (horizon-sq.xlsx). Quick summary: yes for US-only processing/storage for hosted tenants, standard defaults described, and deletion evidence within SLA windows. Full details below.

Answers:

1) US-only processing/storage: Supported. For Hosted API customers we offer region pinning — requests from a pinned tenant are routed to and processed in the selected region (US-East or US-West). Data at rest and compute for that tenant remain in the pinned region unless explicit cross-region failover is invoked (we document failover policies in the attached pack).

2) Default retention: by default we retain request/response payloads for 30 days to support debugging, billing, and quality monitoring. Embeddings or derived artefacts are retained for the same default 30-day window unless a customer enables extended retention settings.

3) Deletion requests (tenant-initiated): We support tenant erasure and offer two modes: immediate purge (best-effort within 72 hours) and scheduled purge (configurable cutoff date). Evidence: after purge we provide an export containing purge job id, timestamps, and a signed confirmation PDF. For hosted contracts with enterprise terms we can commit to a 72-hour SLA for the initial purge job and provide audit artifacts.

4) Backups/snapshots: Backups are stored in-region. We do not replicate backups to other jurisdictions for customers pinned to a single region. Backups are encrypted at rest; for enterprise/private deployments we offer BYOK/KMS integration. For hosted customers we encrypt with provider-managed keys but can enable customer-managed keys for enterprise contracts.

Attachments: HostedAPI_Data_Locality_Answers_v1.2.pdf (detailed answers + flow diagrams), horizon-sq.xlsx (customer questionnaire with cell-level responses).

If you want, Monica (our Customer Security Lead) can jump on a 30-minute call to walk through the PDF and confirm the audit artifacts timeline.

Thanks,

Rajiv — quick follow-up with the clarifications Monica requested and a few UI pointers embedded in the attached PDF and spreadsheet. Highlights below: 

- Console path for retention: Console > Organization > Tenants > [Tenant name] > Data retention settings. That screen shows current retention window and has an "Enable extended retention" toggle (enterprise-only).
- KMS/BYOK: To enable customer-managed keys for backups, customers request an enterprise add-on via the security onboarding form (link in the PDF). Our onboarding team (onboarding@redwood.ai) will coordinate the KMS handshake and acceptance tests.
- Purge SLA: Confirmed — 72-hour purge SLA is available for enterprise-hosted customers under Reserved Capacity / Enterprise agreements. Self-serve tenants receive best-effort purges and we recommend an initial manual purge plus follow-up verification for high-risk timelines. Evidence exports are handled by the Operations Security team (ops-security@redwood.ai); include the tenant id and desired evidence format (CSV + signed confirmation PDF).

I've attached HostedAPI_Data_Locality_Answers_v1.2.pdf with the updated lines and the filled horizon-sq.xlsx. If you'd like a short walkthrough, Monica is happy to join — when is convenient for your team this week?

Thanks,
Stephanie
